questions.q: A deviation drafting bot impressed everyone in a demo but is still unused six months later. Investigators copy its text into the eQMS by hand. Which gap does this show most clearly?
options: The model is not clever enough for this kind of task
Pilot to production: no plan for the output
The site has too few deviations to train on
The demo was too short to convince people
questions.why: Nobody decided where the AI output is stored or who approves it, so the pilot never became part of the real process.

questions.q: Under 21 CFR 211.22, who holds the authority to approve or reject procedures and batches?
options: The quality control unit
The IT department that runs the systems
The AI tool, if it was validated first
The production supervisor on shift
questions.why: The quality control unit has that responsibility and authority. An AI tool can support it but cannot hold it.

questions.q: You are starting an AI project in a GMP plant. When should you first meet the head of quality?
options: At validation, once the tool is built
Only if QA raises a concern
After the first users give feedback
In the first week
questions.why: QA decides whether a tool is ever used in GMP work. Late involvement often means a restart.

questions.q: Which first use of AI is the safest place to start in a GMP site?
options: Automatically releasing batches that pass every test
Closing deviations once no actions are open
Searching SOPs and drafting text a person approves
Approving overdue CAPAs to clear the backlog quickly
questions.why: Search and drafting with human approval keep the GMP decision with a qualified person and build trust with QA.

questions.q: A pilot was tested on 15 clean, hand-picked deviations. What should you do before trusting its results?
options: Add more detailed instructions to the prompt
Test on a random sample of real records
Switch to a larger and more capable model
Ask IT to sign off the pilot results
questions.why: Real GMP records are messy. A random sample shows how the tool behaves on the data it will actually see.

questions.q: Why does adding AI to a deviation process change what an inspector looks at?
options: Inspectors only check AI tools during visits
AI makes deviation records confidential
Inspectors stop reviewing deviations once AI is used
It changes how the evidence is produced
questions.why: In pharma the evidence of control is part of the product. A tool that drafts records changes that evidence, so it must be traceable.
